headline: Bottoming bid meets a hawkish lid: BTC boxed $62-66k into CPI
standfirst: Stagflation-lite tightening: a hawkish-hold Fed prices ~44% odds of a September hike after July payrolls fell, and Hormuz keeps the CPI path hostage. Yet BTC's own demand has turned - five straight ETF inflow days, record long-term supply, washed-out positioning. Neutral-to-constructive over 1-4 weeks: buy the $62k shelf, fade $65-66.5k, let 12 August CPI decide.
body_md:
## State of play

Bitcoin trades around $63,500-$64,000 on Saturday, up roughly 3% on a five-day basis as of Thursday [7] and briefly above $65,000 Friday after the payrolls report before fading into the weekend on darker Hormuz headlines. The tape since the 1 July cycle low near $58,000 [1] has been a grinding, lower-volatility recovery: still a bear market by structure (roughly 50% off the October 2025 peak [1]), but the character has shifted from forced selling to a two-way market. This week delivered the cleanest demand inflection since May: US spot ETFs took in about $865m over five straight sessions [2], July nonfarm payrolls fell 23,000 and knocked the odds of a September Fed hike from ~67% at month-end [1] to ~44% [3], and gold printed a two-month high while BTC held the 200-week moving-average shelf - the debasement bid is finally showing up in both metals and crypto. Against that: the Fed remains on a hawkish hold with three dissenters who wanted to hike [4], CPI is still running 3.5% year-on-year with the Strait of Hormuz as the wildcard, and credit stress is building inside the AI complex while index volatility sleeps. This is a first report - no prior calls to score; today's base case (late-cycle stagflation-lite tightening with a crypto-specific bottoming bid, neutral-to-mildly-constructive inside $61.5k-$66.5k) is the baseline future editions will be graded against.

## Overall picture

### Regime call: stagflation-lite with a crypto-specific bid

Name the regime **late-cycle stagflation-lite tightening with endogenous financial stress**: an energy shock keeps inflation above target while the labor market rolls over, leaving a hawkish Fed poised to hike even as credit markets begin pricing the AI-capex complex. The three variables that decide the next 1-4 weeks, in order: (1) the 12 August CPI and the September-hike repricing it triggers; (2) Hormuz - whether the Iran-Oman shipping corridor hardens into actual barrels or collapses back to closure; (3) persistence of the ETF flow turn [1][2]. Directional bias: **neutral-to-mildly-bullish** inside a $61.5k-$66.5k box, with asymmetric upside if CPI resolves soft and a weekly close below $60k as the hard exit. Conviction: medium, 6/10 - the demand-side evidence has improved materially, but the macro lid is real and binary.

The mechanism in one line: BTC is no longer trading as a high-beta AI proxy - it decoupled from the semiconductor unwind through July, holding $63-64k while the SOX entered a bear market [1] - so macro now hits it through the real-rates/hike-odds channel rather than the equity-beta channel, while its own flow base sets the floor.

### Macro: labor cracks under an energy lid

July payrolls: -23,000 versus +83,000 consensus, with June revised down to +20,000 and May to +63,000; the 12-month average now sits at just +34,000. The unemployment rate slipped to 4.1% for the wrong reason - participation fell to 61.4%, a multi-decade low outside the pandemic era - and wage growth cooled to 3.2% year-on-year, the weakest since May 2021 [3]. That is the first hard confirmation of labor-side disinflation in months, and markets treated it as such: equity futures rallied, yields dropped, gold jumped 2.4%, and September-hike odds fell to 44% from 67% [1][3].

The Fed is not there yet. The 29 July FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% on a 9-3 vote, with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissenting in favor of a 25bp hike; the statement flags inflation "elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal, in part reflecting supply shocks" including energy, and commits to "deliver price stability" [4]. Several officials have since spoken in favor of hiking as soon as September if price pressures do not ease [3], and futures still price roughly two hikes by year-end as of late July [1]. June CPI fell 0.4% month-on-month but still sits 3.5% year-on-year - well above the pre-war 2.4% pace - and consensus for 12 August is a modest +0.1% MoM and ~3.4% YoY, with the late-July oil re-escalation a pure upside risk to that path.

### Rates and credit: the tightening the VIX is not showing

The bond market is doing the Fed's tightening for it. The 10-year yield eased to ~4.65% into the jobs report after touching 4.75% on 31 July, and the 30-year recently reached its highest level since 2007 [1]. The rise has been driven substantially by inflation expectations tied to the energy shock [1] - the hawkish kind of backup for a non-yielding asset. So far, primary demand has absorbed the supply: the early-August refunding auctions cleared without distress even as Bitwise's foreign-demand index flags pressure on Japan and China to liquidate Treasury reserves to fund a rising oil import bill [1].

Credit is where the stress is genuine. Oracle's 5-year CDS reached its widest since 2008, 1-year implied volatilities across the hyperscalers made new highs, and leading credit indicators - private credit funds, leveraged loans, BDCs - are all weakening; the SOX corrected -23.6% from its peak (roughly $1.5tn of value since late June) and margin debt sits at a record $1.42tn [1]. Equity indices, meanwhile, keep printing records (DAX, FTSE MIB, TSX all at highs this week) - a market split between index complacency and single-name credit stress. For BTC the transmission is two-sided: a hyperscaler credit event would initially drag crypto via forced liquidity ("sell what you can"), but Bitwise argues such a capitulation would force the monetary/fiscal response that starts the next crypto bull leg, with BTC anticipating the easing ahead of equities [1]. That asymmetry is why this desk treats credit stress as a both-way risk, not a pure bear input.

### Global: hiking ECB, normalising BoJ, stalled Chinese M2

Europe: the ECB delivered its first hike in three years in June and held in July; markets price one further hike by year-end with a smaller probability of a second. The 10-year Bund sits near 3.13%, German flash inflation re-accelerated to 2.8% in July, yet German industrial production and orders keep beating and the DAX is at a record - Europe is absorbing higher rates on fiscal momentum. Bitwise's cross-sovereign read confirms yields grinding higher across Japan and Europe alongside multi-decade US longs [1].

Japan: the BoJ held at 1.00% but July minutes show board members expecting a significant H2 inflation acceleration, keeping a September hike live; the 10-year JGB is at 2.80% (+131bp YoY) and the 30-year near 3.92% (reference 8 tracks this complex). Household spending fell 3.3% in June and the authorities have already spent reserves defending the yen (FX reserves at a 16-month low). The swing risk: a BoJ hike landing on top of a dovish US repricing would whipsaw the yen and force another carry unwind - an explicit tail risk for all risk assets, BTC included.

China: M2 expansion has stalled - Bitwise identifies it as the monetary headwind behind gold's July correction and, by extension, a missing tailwind for crypto [1]. Chinese institutional money is rotating into gold-backed products as a tech-volatility hedge. July activity data land on 14 August; a stimulus surprise is the positive tail for global risk appetite.

Net liquidity: the Fed maintains its ample-reserves posture [4] - the QT era is functionally over - but dollar liquidity is being drained at the margin through the oil-import channel, with exporters accumulating claims and importers burning FX [1]. Historically BTC trades global liquidity impulses with a lag measured in quarters; Bitwise's read is that BTC has been leading instead - the "macro canary" - with July resilience anticipating eventual policy easing [1]. Treat that as a thesis, not an established fact.

### Geopolitics: the Hormuz transmission loop

The Iran conflict is the swing variable for inflation and therefore for the Fed. The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed (fewer than 10 vessels per day, pre-memorandum levels), with Brent briefly above $100 in July after Iran struck a Qatari LNG tanker and the US hit 80+ targets; a Bab al-Mandeb escalation adds freight pressure [1]. Last week whipsawed: mid-week, reports of an interim US-Iran deal and an Iran-Oman shipping corridor dropped crude roughly 10%, then reports Iran may bar US and Israeli vessels and demand compensation sent it back up. Transmission to BTC runs three channels: (i) oil to CPI to hike odds to real-rate pressure (dominant, negative); (ii) safe-haven bid - currently expressed in gold ($4,343, +28% YoY, well off January's $5,608 peak), though gold and BTC traded in tandem last week; (iii) energy costs squeezing miners, feeding the ~100k BTC of potential miner supply 10x Research expects as operations pivot to AI [6]. Until Hormuz resolves, every CPI print carries a geopolitical error bar.

### Demand flows: the turn

The week's cleanest bullish input. US spot BTC ETFs: +$170.1m (3 Aug), +$211.5m (4 Aug), +$244.4m (5 Aug), +$137.6m (6 Aug), +$101.7m (7 Aug) - about $865m over five straight positive sessions [2]. Context matters: since the cumulative-flow peak in early May, the complex bled $8.44bn across 59 sessions, with net additions on only 18 of them [7]. Last week is the first sustained reversal of that regime.

| Fund group | Week 27-31 Jul | Week 3-7 Aug |
| --- | --- | --- |
| US spot BTC ETFs [2] | -$61.5m | +$865.3m |
| IBIT alone [2] | -$66.5m | +$693.5m |
| US spot ETH ETFs (4-6 Aug) [2] | mixed | +$206.0m |

IBIT took ~$693m of the weekly total and GBTC's bleed has effectively stopped [2]. ETH funds confirm the intra-crypto risk-appetite read: Farside's sister table shows accelerating inflows of +$53.1m, +$60.8m and +$92.1m from 4-6 August led by ETHA, with staking-enabled wrappers now active in the product set. Caveats: one week does not end a regime - BlockScholes' 20-day rolling flow has only just turned [7]; the flow-vs-price divergence (ETFs buying while spot grinds sideways) suggests creations are absorbing seller supply rather than chasing price; and part of the impulse may be custody-scare driven after a hardware-wallet exploit, a link desk coverage flags as unproven. Net institutional demand (global ETPs + treasury companies minus new supply) is mean-reverting from its lowest level since late 2022 [1] - that is the structural flow argument for the next 1-3 months.

### Policy: Clarity pushed to September

The Clarity Act will not pass before the Senate's August recess. Leadership confirmed a September sequence, with a first procedural cloture vote possible 15 September; the bill needs 60 votes and may not yet have 50, with an ethics provision targeting senior officials' crypto ventures the main sticking point, plus stablecoin rewards and Agriculture language [6]. Prediction-market odds on 2026 enactment have compressed to the mid-teens [7]. Near-term flow impact: mildly negative, in that it removes a near-dated positive catalyst; tail risk: a failed September cloture would price out the market-structure premium entirely. Elsewhere: OFAC widened Iran-related sanctions to two crypto exchanges, and product expansion continues (T. Rowe Price launched the first actively managed multi-token spot crypto ETF in mid-July).

### Treasury companies: forced-seller risk down, buying not yet back

Strategy sold 3,588 BTC (~$216m) in early July - its largest sale since abandoning the never-sell stance - but has since rebuilt USD cash to 22+ months of dividend coverage, committed to holding at least 12 months of reserves, and seen its STRC perpetual preferred recover toward par; Bitwise reads forced-liquidation risk as averted, with the "digital credit engine" positioned to restart purchases via new STRC issuance [1]. 10x Research still expects additional supply from treasury-company unwinds [6]. The broader DAT cohort is dormant - sector trading volumes at the 2.7th percentile of their 1-year range [1] and at least one would-be treasury deal (Trump Media's CRO arrangement) scrapped this week. Net: neutral, improving at the margin - the overhang is capped even if the bid is not yet active.

### Internals and on-chain: bottoming arithmetic

The on-chain picture is unusually consistent for a market this deep in a bear phase. Roughly 4.5mn BTC have been redistributed since the October top - inside the 4.5-5.0mn band seen across prior cycle lows; days with supply-in-profit below the -1 sigma band total 107 versus 112-172 at historical bottoms; long-term holder supply sits at a record high (~14.7mn BTC) [1][6]. K33 flagged in early July that more than half of supply was held at a loss - a threshold that preceded cycle bottoms by 13-31 days in 2017, 2018 and 2022 [6]; that signal is now stale in calendar terms but unresolved in price terms. Cost-basis levels define the swing map:

| Level | Price | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| True market mean | $76k | Macro risk-on confirmation [1] |
| STH cost basis | $69k | Local bull/bear delineator [1] |
| Weekly EMA20 / BB midline | ~$68.8-69.1k | Macro resistance confluence |
| 200-week MA | $62.4k | Current demand shelf [1] |
| Realised price | $53.3k | Terminal valuation floor [1] |

Counterpoints: the realised cap is still contracting (capital-destruction regime) and SOPR hovers near 1 - holders exit at breakeven, which is why each rally into $64-65k meets supply [1]. Volume is the wildcard: spot volume at the 0.3rd percentile of 3 years means thin books where ETF-scale flows move price disproportionately in both directions [1]. Stablecoins (~$279.5bn market cap) are the dry powder. Internals: BTC dominance 58.6%, altseason index 51, ETH/BTC at a 3-month high near 0.030 - capital is barbelled into the two majors with no alt breadth: pre-broadening, not alt-season.

### Positioning and sentiment: washed out, not euphoric

Perp funding is effectively flat (+0.0066%/8h as of 3 August). As of early July - flag as pre-re-escalation and stale - CME futures open interest sat at a 32-month low, the CME term structure at its tightest since early 2023, and six-month put skew at the fourth-highest reading on record, with precedents only in June and November 2022, both near cycle bottoms. This week futures turnover ran at a record multiple of spot volumes - leverage is concentrated in perps while cash markets stay thin, so squeezes propagate fast but there is no speculative froth to unwind. Sentiment: Fear & Greed at 30 (fear), recovering from 22 (extreme fear) a month ago - contrarian-supportive without being crowded. The market is two-sided at the margin: one large European bank disclosed cutting its IBIT position ~94% and adding put protection even as aggregate ETF flows turned positive [2].

## What changed this week

First run - no prior reports; these are the deltas that defined the past seven days:

1. **Rate odds flipped.** September-hike pricing collapsed from ~67% (late July) [1] to ~44% on the payrolls miss; October sits near 58% [3]. The hike-is-inevitable narrative cracked on labor data.
2. **Flows flipped.** -$61.5m the week of 27 July to +$865.3m the week of 3 August - the sharpest weekly turn since the May outflow regime began [2][7].
3. **Hormuz round-tripped.** Corridor-deal optimism (crude -10%) mid-week, re-escalation (Iran threatening vessel restrictions and compensation) by Friday. The binary rolls forward unresolved.
4. **Clarity slipped.** No pre-recess vote; cloture sequence now 15 September at the earliest, with 2026 passage odds in the mid-teens [6][7].
5. **Debasement complex tightened.** Gold +2.4% Friday to a two-month high while BTC held - gold and BTC traded in tandem on the dovish repricing, an early hint BTC's correlation regime may be shifting from risk asset toward debasement hedge. Watch it.
6. **Strategy de-risked.** From active seller ($216m BTC sale) to 22 months of dividend cash coverage [1] - the single largest forced-selling overhang of this bear market has been defused.

## Consensus and discrepancies

**Where credible desks agree:** the September FOMC is live; energy is the inflation swing factor; the AI-capex unwind is the key financial-stability risk; and BTC's bottoming process is well advanced (10x Research, K33, Grayscale and Bitwise all land here from different data [1][6]).

**Where they split:** 10x Research favors longs and says a monthly close above $63,000 confirms the bear-market bottom [6]; BlockScholes' flow analytics treat the complex as still in a net-outflow regime until proven otherwise, with the 20-day rolling flow only just turning [7]; Bitwise keeps short-term downside risk elevated pending a possible TradFi capitulation, arguing BTC then leads the recovery [1]. Grayscale's Pandl sees the bottom arriving earlier than the classic four-year cycle implies [6]. Inside the FOMC itself, three dissenters wanted to hike now versus a hold majority [4]. Northlight's read of the jobs report - a "game changer" re-injecting labor-market risk into a hike-consensus [3] - sits against officials like Cook who still call inflation too high.

**Where market pricing disagrees with the narrative:** equity-index volatility is asleep while hyperscaler CDS prints records and margin debt hits $1.42tn [1]; BTC decoupled from the semiconductor rout that its historical risk-asset correlation says it should have joined [1]; and gold is up 28% YoY while BTC is down ~50% - debasement money has clearly preferred metal so far.

**Where this report departs:** more constructive than the BlockScholes flow-regime read (the five-day inflow streak plus the LTH bid deserves weight), less aggressive than 10x's bottom confirmation (a monthly close above $63k is necessary, not sufficient, with CPI unresolved). The flow turn is real until a hot CPI proves otherwise - but it does not yet justify chasing above $65k.

## Actionable theses

| Scenario | Prob | Path | Deciding catalysts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base - range chop | ~50% | $60.5k-$66.5k consolidation; monthly close >$63k matures bottoming indicators [6] | CPI in line; Hormuz status quo |
| Bull - CPI relief | ~25% | Reclaim $65-66.5k, test $68.5-69.5k STH band [1] | Headline <=3.3% YoY; Sep-hike odds <30%; weekly ETF inflows >$1bn |
| Bear - stagflation bite | ~25% | Lose $61.5k, target $59.5-60k, risk $57-58k [1] | Headline >=3.6% or core re-acceleration; Brent >$105 sustained |

**T1 - Buy the 200-week shelf.** Entry zone $61.5-62.5k (July recovery floor plus the $62.4k 200-week MA [1]). Invalidation: daily close below $59.4k. Targets: $65k, then $68.5k. Catalyst: 12 August CPI resolving soft and flow persistence above ~$150m/day. Horizon: 2-4 weeks. This is the highest-conviction expression of the base case.

**T2 - Breakout confirmation, not anticipation.** Trigger: daily close above $66.5k (July high zone) with the week's ETF flows >$1bn [2]. Target: $69k STH cost basis [1], where the position should be trimmed - regime change requires holding above $69k, not touching it. Invalidation: fallback below $63.9k. Horizon: 1-3 weeks.

**T3 - Event risk into 12 August CPI.** With put skew still elevated from July's spike, hedging with outright puts is expensive - express protection as put spreads or calendar structures instead. A hot print likely takes out $61.5k before the auction finds real bids; the plan is to stand aside and reassess at $59.5-60k with a volume-flush signature, not to knife-catch at first touch.

**T4 - Relative value: BTC over the AI complex.** Premise: BTC decoupled from the SOX unwind in July [1] while hyperscaler credit stress builds; long BTC against AI-equity beta captures the divergence. The trade dies - and flips into an opportunity - on a capitulation flush, when correlations spike back to one and BTC is sold for liquidity; per the Bitwise canary framework [1], that flush is the higher-conviction entry for the next leg.

**What would prove this report wrong:** a weekly close below $60k (base case dead, bear scenario active); conversely, a daily close above $69.5k on flows (bear case dead, regime change underway). A confirmed Hormuz reopening with Brent back below $80 would upgrade the bull probability within days; a hyperscaler credit event would suspend all swing theses pending the liquidity response.
